title: The sailings I talk people out of
subtitle: Saying no is the most useful thing an advisor does, and easily the least popular.

text: A commission I don't earn costs less than a client I disappoint.
sub: I'm paid after you sail. If the voyage is wrong, I've spent months on a booking that ends in a polite email and no second trip. That maths is not subtle.

items.head: The famous ship in high August
items.body: Right ship, wrong fortnight. The same itinerary in late September is a different holiday entirely.

items.head: Seven ports in nine days
items.body: You will see harbours and coach parks. Sea days are not filler - they are why the rest works.

items.head: The tender-heavy itinerary
items.body: Moderate swell suspends tendering. Two of your best ports become a view from the rail.

items.head: The bargain suite, wrong deck
items.body: Under the pool deck, or forward on a small ship in winter. The price is telling you something.

right.label: Editing
items: Removes what won't earn its keep

quote: Honest counsel on ships, seasons and itineraries - including which celebrated ones to skip.

text: No isn't a lost sale. It's what makes the next yes worth anything.
sub: You cannot be candid about a ship on Monday and sell it on Friday to someone plainly unsuited to it. The whole practice rests on that one line holding.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Or send me the sailing you are half-decided on. If I'd talk you out of it, I'll tell you exactly why, and what I'd put in its place.
